correctness.rationale: For all characteristic-two fields, noncommutative dimension-three two-step multiplication has a two-by-two matrix B with b+c nonzero; P=((0,d/(b+c)),(a/(b+c),1)) satisfies P^T B+BP=B, producing a nonzero-square derivation and proper local projection. In dimension four, B is nonsingular and the nine derivation equations give P=alpha I+beta E_zx, square scalar zero, and three independent central shears. Pointwise tests at y,z,y+z,x,x+y force every local map to that form. Finite-field exhaustive independent checks over q=2,4,8 confirm dimensions and all smaller noncommutative tensors.

value.rationale: The invariant is the natural sharp dimension at which noncommutative two-step Zinbiel algebras become rigid against pointwise derivation matching. The result combines a universal three-dimensional obstruction with an indecomposable four-dimensional witness and full five-parameter derivation classification, separating characteristic-two behavior from the known characteristic-zero results and commutative low-dimensional cases.
